Talk records a spoken request and puts the words in the text field
for you to check before sending. It needs whisper.cpp's
whisper-server (brew install whisper.cpp, or set
RUNEBENDER_WHISPER_SERVER) and a speech model saved as model.bin
in a model folder whose name starts with whisper. The button is
hidden until both are found.

Chat needs the desktop application on macOS or Linux.

### What Is Not Here

For an external conversation connected to the live editor, start with
[MCP](/docs/mcp.html). Neither Chat nor MCP currently provides
complete glyph generation from a description. Kerning and spacing models
are named in font-ml and not built.


## Set up local AI
https://runebender.org/docs/local-ai-setup.html

Install two programs, clone one repo, and train your first model in five minutes.

### What You Need

A mid-range computer: an Apple Silicon laptop, a Linux PC with a gaming GPU, or a plain CPU with patience. Rust stable from [rustup.rs](https://rustup.rs). About 1 GB of disk for the chat model, more for the larger sizes.

Everything runs on your machine. No account, no API key, and nothing is sent anywhere.

### Install Two Programs

runebender is the editor. font-ml runs and trains the models. Build font-ml with metal on macOS, cuda on Linux with a working NVIDIA toolkit, and no feature flag otherwise.

    cargo install --git https://github.com/fontgarden/runebender
    cargo install --git https://github.com/eliheuer/font-ml --features metal
    cargo install --git https://github.com/eliheuer/font-ml --features cuda
    cargo install --git https://github.com/eliheuer/font-ml

The last three commands are alternatives. Check both programs answer:

    runebender --help
    font-ml tasks

font-ml tasks is authoritative: only tasks marked ready are usable. The demos use draw, train-draw, bolden, and train.

### Clone the Demo Repo

[runebender-local-ai-demo](https://github.com/eliheuer/runebender-local-ai-demo) holds everything the demos need: a small font family made for training, scripts, node graphs, and a checked-in copy of the first model in case your training run fails. Large models are never in the repo; a script downloads them from a named URL and checks the hash.

    git clone https://github.com/eliheuer/runebender-local-ai-demo
    cd runebender-local-ai-demo

Work through the numbered folders in order. Each has a README.

| Demo | What you do |
| --- | --- |
| 01-draw-from-text | Train a shapes model inside the editor, then drag a box, type "star", and the local AI shapes tool fills it |
| 02-train-and-bolden | Train a model on the Shapes font, then bolden a new shape in the editor |
| 03-chat-model | Download a small open chat model from Hugging Face and ask it about the font |
| 04-nodes | The same train and bolden steps as a node graph |
| 05-real-font | The bolden loop on Virtua Grotesk, a real typeface |

### Train Your First Model

    runebender fonts/Shapes.ufo

Open any glyph. In the toolbar, hold the shapes button and pick **Local AI Shapes**. The right panel shows the Local AI Shapes section: with no model yet it offers Quick or Thorough training and two buttons, Train From This Font and Train From the Sample Shapes. Click the second. The panel shows the time left and what the model draws right now; a quick run takes about twelve minutes on a laptop GPU, a thorough one about thirty.

When it finishes, the panel lists the shapes the model knows. Click one, then drag a box on the glyph. The model fills the box with a ghost. Enter keeps it as one undo step, Tab asks for another option, Esc drops it. Drag the box's handles to resize it and the shape is drawn again to fit.

The model knows only the shapes in the font and the words for them. A glyph named circle taught it "circle"; "heart" is not in the list until you draw one and click Add This Font's Shapes, which adds it to the model in about two minutes. That is the whole lesson: your drawings in, a model out, the model used from a tool.

The demo repo has the same run as a script, 01-draw-from-text/train.sh, and 01-draw-from-text/get-base-model.sh, which downloads a trained base from the repo's releases with a checksum, to skip the wait.

### Where Models Live

A model is a directory. The editor reads them from ~/Runebender/models, a visible folder you can open in Finder and drop a model into, sorted by kind: shapes/, bolden/, chat/. A font's own models live beside it in MyFont.models/, so they travel with the font. RUNEBENDER_MODELS overrides the root for one run, and ~/.runebender/model_paths or RUNEBENDER_MODEL_PATHS lists extra folders, one per line. The older ~/.runebender/models is still read.

| Kind | Files | Comes from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shapes model | config.json, weights.safetensors, vocab.txt, manifest.json | The Local AI shapes tool trains it from a UFO |
| Bolden model | config.json, weights.safetensors, vocab.txt | font-ml run train from two masters |
| Chat model | one .gguf, optional model.json | You download it; the demo script fetches Qwen3 from Hugging Face |

The kinds are different artifacts. A chat model does not draw shapes, and a shapes model does not talk.

### Recover from Common Failures

- **No model in the editor:** the directory must sit under ~/Runebender/models// or beside the font in MyFont.models//. Check RUNEBENDER_MODELS if you set it.
- **font-ml is missing:** Cargo's bin directory is not on PATH.
- **A GPU request fails:** add --device cpu, or rebuild font-ml without the feature flag.
- **Training fails:** run ./01-draw-from-text/get-base-model.sh in the demo repo and carry on with the editor steps.
- **A download fails:** the script resumes where it stopped. Run it again.
- **A chat answer is wrong:** expected at 0.6B. The script fetches 1.7B and 4B too; 4B is what the Chat panel was built with.

Continue with [Local Models](/docs/local-models.html) for what the editor does with a model, and [Type design with agents](/docs/type-design.html) for the working method.


## Tutorial: Draw a Glyph
https://runebender.org/docs/tutorial-first-glyph.html

Draw a letter, space it, see it in a word, and save it. About twenty minutes.

### Before You Start

You need Runebender installed and a font to work in. With a font open
and saved, press Cmd+N for a new one. There is no dialog: Runebender
writes Untitled.ufo in the same folder as the current font, with
Google Fonts metrics and the Latin Core set as empty encoded glyphs.

Put the folder under version control first. It costs one command and
makes every step below undoable.

    git init && git add . && git commit -m 'Empty font'

### 1. Open a Glyph

Type H in the Search glyphs field. Double-click the cell.

The editor opens on an empty glyph with its metrics drawn around it:
the baseline, the x-height, the cap height, and two vertical lines for
the sidebearings.

### 2. Draw the Left Stem

Take the pen tool.

1. Click at the baseline, a little right of the left sidebearing.
2. Click straight up at the cap height.
3. Click right by about 80 units.
4. Click back down to the baseline.
5. Click the first point again to close the contour.

You have a rectangle. Switch to the select tool and drag its points
until the width looks right at a glance. Numbers come later; the eye
first.

### 3. Reuse It

Rather than draw the second stem, copy the first: select all four
points with Cmd+A, then Cmd+D to duplicate.
The copy lands 20 units up and to the right, and it is selected. Move
it into place with the X and Y fields in the Coordinates section of
the right panel, so it stays level.

Draw the crossbar the same way, a rectangle between the two stems, a
little above the middle. The optical centre of a letter sits above the
mathematical centre.

### 4. Clean Up

Three commands, in this order, before you go further.

Cleanup:
- Path → Remove Overlap: Cmd+Shift+O. Merges the three rectangles into one outline.
- Path → Correct Path Direction: Cmd+Shift+R. Sets the direction the fill rule expects.
- Path → Tidy Up Paths: Cmd+Shift+T. Drops any zero-length segments the overlap left.

### 5. Space It

The Glyph section of the right panel holds the Width, LSB and RSB
fields. Open the section, then set
both sidebearings to the same number to start; something near 80 units
for a capital H at 1000 UPM.

Spacing is judged in company, not alone.

### 6. See It in a Word

Take the text tool and type HHH. Then HOH if you have drawn an O,
or leave it as three Hs.

The rhythm should be even: the white inside the H and the white
between two Hs want to look like the same amount of space. Change LSB
and RSB in the Glyph section until they do. Everything you change
shows up in the line.

Space glyphs in company. A glyph on its own shows little.

### 7. Check the Curves

An H needs no curve checking, but find the control now. Open the
Curves section in the right panel and turn on Curvature Comb. It is flat on
straight segments. On curves, a kink invisible at text size shows as a
break.

### 8. Save

Cmd+S. The middle of the footer changes from Not saved to
Saved.

Now look at what changed:

    git diff --stat

One glyph file, and the metrics if you touched them. That is the
argument for a source format made of small files.

### Next

Draw an O, and you meet curves, overshoot, and extremes. Then an
accented glyph, which you build rather than draw: see
[Components and Anchors](/docs/components.html) and the recipes in
[Workflows](/docs/workflows.html).


## Workflows
https://runebender.org/docs/workflows.html

Short recipes for jobs that cross several parts of the editor.

### Build an Accented Glyph

1. Draw the base letter and the mark as separate glyphs.
2. Put an anchor on the base where the mark belongs, and a matching
one on the mark.
3. Open the accented glyph. In the Shapes panel of the left rail, type
each name in the Base glyph field and press Add.
4. The mark places itself from the anchors, and stays put when you
edit the base.
5. Run Generate in the Features section of the grid view to write the
mark feature from those anchors.

See [Components and Anchors](/docs/components.html) and
[Feature Code](/docs/features.html).

### Draw From a Skeleton

1. With the pen tool, draw open paths down the middle of the strokes.
2. Select them, or select nothing to take the whole glyph.
3. In the Path Operations section, type a weight in Stroke width and
press Enter.
4. Clean up with Remove Overlap and Correct Path Direction.

Copy the skeleton to a named glyph layer first, with Copy to layer in
the Layers section. Then you can expand it again at a different weight
instead of redrawing.

See [Paths and Filters](/docs/paths.html).

### Add a Weight

1. Open the designspace. Set the axis sliders to the new weight.
2. Type a name in Source name and press Add source in the Masters
section. Runebender adds an interpolated source, and Save writes
its new UFO.
3. Draw the new master, then use the axis sliders to check what falls
between.
4. Use the Compare section to find glyphs that no longer interpolate.

See [Masters and Interpolation](/docs/masters.html) and
[Checking a Font](/docs/checking.html).

### Space and Kern a Font

1. Set widths and sidebearings on the control characters first, with
the Width, LSB and RSB fields in the Glyph section.
2. If the source has metric keys, run Glyph → Update Metrics to apply
every key.
3. Put glyphs that kern alike into groups, so one value covers many
pairs.
4. Set pairs with the First, Second and Value fields in the Kerning
section of the grid view.
5. Check the result in real words with the text tool.

See [Spacing and Kerning](/docs/spacing.html).

### Start an Arabic Font

1. Name the positional forms by convention: beh.init, beh.medi,
beh.fina, with beh as the isolated form.
2. Put entry and exit anchors on the joining edges.
3. Run Generate in the Features section. It writes init, medi,
fina, and curs from those names and anchors.
4. Press Apply, then type words with the text tool and read them.
5. Run Glyph → Check Joining. It selects every form whose connecting
stroke misses the font's common band.
6. When a word comes out wrong, use the Shaping section to turn
features off one at a time, or to change the script and language.

See [Text and Shaping](/docs/text.html).

### Trace a Drawing

1. Glyph → Place Image… puts a bitmap behind the glyph.
2. Glyph → Trace Image… converts it to contours. It is undoable.
3. Tidy the result: Optimize, then Add Extremes, then Correct Path
Direction.

For a cleaner result, trace to get the shape and then redraw over it
with the pen tool, using the image as a reference rather than as the
outline.

See [Glyphs](/docs/glyphs.html).

### Make a Variable Font

1. Draw the masters and keep them compatible as you go.
2. Use the Compare section and fix what it reports.
3. Run File → Export.

Export compiles the open document with fontc inside Runebender,
including edits you have not saved. It writes
exports/<name>.ttf beside the source. See
Exporting.

### Work on a Font From a Terminal

Runebender reloads files changed on disk, so a script and the editor
can share a font.

1. Keep the editor open on the designspace.
2. Run your script over the UFO.
3. The editor picks up the change.

Keep the source in version control, so a script that goes wrong is one
git checkout away from being undone.


## Shortcuts
https://runebender.org/docs/shortcuts.html

Every keyboard command, by menu. On Windows and Linux, read Cmd as Ctrl.

### File

File:
- Cmd+N: New font
- Cmd+O: Open
- Cmd+S: Save
- Cmd+Shift+S: Save as
- Cmd+Alt+E: Export
- Cmd+Q: Quit

### Edit

Edit:
- Cmd+Z: Undo
- Cmd+Shift+Z: Redo
- Cmd+C: Copy
- Cmd+V: Paste
- Cmd+A: Select all points
- Cmd+Alt+A: Deselect all points
- Cmd+Alt+Shift+I: Invert selection
- Tab / Shift+Tab: Step the point selection through the contour

### Glyph

The Glyph menu has no keys.

### Path

Path:
- Cmd+Shift+T: Tidy up paths
- Cmd+Shift+O: Remove overlap
- Cmd+Shift+R: Correct path direction
- Cmd+Alt+Shift+R: Reverse contours
- Cmd+Shift+H: Flip horizontal
- Cmd+Shift+V: Flip vertical
- Cmd+D: Duplicate selection
- Cmd+Shift+D: Duplicate and repeat

### View

View:
- Cmd+0: Zoom to fit
- Cmd+T: Cycle theme
- Escape: Back to the overview
- Hold Space: Pan, and preview the filled glyph without points or guides

The rest of the View menu has no key: masters, sorting, sample
strings, grid, and the measure overlays.

### Tools

Tools:
- V: Select
- P: Pen
- B: Hyperbezier Pen
- U: Rectangle
- O: Ellipse
- E: Knife
- M: Measure

The other tools have no key. Pick them in the toolbar.

### Text Mode

Caret:
- Left, Right: Move the caret visually, not by storage order.
- Up, Down: Move a line.
- Home, End: Go to the visual edges of the line.
- Backspace, Delete: Delete, re-shaping Arabic around the caret.
- Enter: Line break.

### Menus Without Shortcuts

Everything in the menus works whether or not it has a key. The Path
and Filter menus hold many operations that do not: booleans,
extremes, rounding, rotation, harmonize, balance, optimize, curve
and metaball conversion, offset, extrude, roughen, round corners,
and slant.


## File Format
https://runebender.org/docs/format.html

Runebender edits UFO in place. It writes standard data where a standard exists, and namespaced keys where none does.

### Sources

Runebender opens .designspace files and .ufo directories. It
treats any other directory as a UFO, so it does not open a folder
that only holds sources. It saves in the same format, in place.

It can also import Glyphs, Glyphs Package, compiled fonts, and basic
single-master Babelfont packages into UFO. See
[Opening and Saving](/docs/opening.html) for the supported data and limitations.

UFO is a directory of files, so a font source works with version
control. Commit your sources and you can see, review, and undo a day's
drawing the way you would any other change.

Runebender writes to your files. Keep them in version control and
work on copies while the editor is alpha.

### Standard Data

Standard UFO data:
- Outlines: GLIF contours, points, and components.
- Anchors: Standard GLIF anchors.
- Kerning: kerning.plist and groups.plist, per master.
- public.kern: Group names follow the standard prefixes.
- public.background: The background layer, saved with the font.
- public.postscriptNames: Production names. Export does not apply them: the exported font keeps the working glyph names.
- Features: features.fea, one file per master, holding prefixes, classes, and features.
- Layers: Named glyph layers from the Layers section are ordinary UFO layers.
- Designspace: Axes and sources. The Masters section adds, renames, moves, reorders and removes sources.
- com.github.googlei18n.ufo2ft.colorPalettes: The CPAL palette for colour fonts.

### Glyphs Compatibility

Sources that came out of Glyphs keep their smart component data.
Runebender reads and writes the glyphsLib keys rather than inventing
its own.

glyphsLib keys:
- com.schriftgestaltung.Glyphs.smartComponentAxes: The axes a smart component carries.
- com.schriftgestaltung.Glyphs.componentsSmartComponentValues: Where a placed component sits in those axes.
- com.schriftgestaltung.Glyphs.glyph.leftMetricsKey: Metric keys, left and right. See Spacing and Kerning.

### Runebender Keys

Anything Runebender needs that UFO does not define lives under its own
namespace. Another editor ignores these keys, and the rest of the
source still reads correctly.

com.runebender keys:
- savedFilters: Filters saved in the left panel.
- annotations: Notes left on a glyph.
- masks: The contours of a glyph that are masks.
- hoiIntermediate: Per-point intermediate positions for higher-order interpolation.
- partSelection: Which part of a smart component is in use.

### Hyperbeziers

A hyperbezier contour is defined by its on-curve points, with the
control points solved rather than placed. Runebender marks these
contours in GLIF with an identifier that starts with
hyperbezier.

An editor that does not know the identifier reads the points as
ordinary curve points, so the file stays valid. Use Path → Hyperbezier
to Cubic before handing a source to a tool that needs plain cubics.

### What Survives a Round Trip

Runebender aims to write files another tool can read. Standard data stays standard. Glyphs-compatible data uses the glyphsLib
keys rather than a private spelling. Anything genuinely new sits under
com.runebender, which another editor ignores while leaving the rest of
the source intact.

Two things to know before handing a source on:

1. Hyperbezier contours read as ordinary curves elsewhere. Convert
them if the receiving tool will re-save the file.
2. Masks are a Runebender idea. Run Glyph → Bake Masks so the
subtraction is real in the outlines.


## Source format preservation
https://runebender.org/docs/source-format-allowlist.html

The UFO and Designspace fields preserved or explicitly rejected by the editor.

This reference lists the source-format fields accepted by the filesystem UFO/Designspace adapter and their authoritative owners.
Anything not listed here must either remain opaque under the listed boundary payload or fail before Project construction.
It must never disappear during load, canonical edit, save, Save As or reopen.

## Ownership labels

- **Canonical** means the live document owns the editable value and export reconstructs its UFO or Designspace representation.
- **Layer preservation** means the value is attached to a stable glyph-layer or object identity because Babelfont cannot represent it faithfully.
- **SourceFormatData** means the value is source-wide format data required for lossless serialization but is not editable canonical state.
The record is glyph-free and does not retain a complete Norad font.
- **Filesystem preservation** means raw bytes or exact paths outside Norad's supported object model.

## UFO allowlist

| UFO field family | Current authoritative owner | Export rule |
|---|---|---|
| Source destination and dirty/save status | Project source shell | Save and Save As publish only to checked destinations; source removal never deletes the UFO. |
| metainfo.plist: creator, format version and minor version | SourceFormatData | Preserve the decoded values exactly. |
| fontinfo.plist: family/style, copyright/trademark, designer/manufacturer/license/description/version/unique/sample/PostScript/typographic/WWS names | Canonical CanonicalFontInfo::names | Clear from the preservation payload and reconstruct from the canonical value. |
| fontinfo.plist: units per em, ascender, descender, x-height, cap height and italic angle | Canonical CanonicalFontInfo::metrics | Retain exact f64 values and reject nonfinite values or negative units per em. |
| fontinfo.plist: supported hhea and OS/2 metrics, head flags, embedding and selection flags, weight/width class, vendor ID, note and major/minor version | Canonical CanonicalFontInfo OpenType fields | Clear from the preservation payload and reconstruct from the canonical value. |
| Every other field represented by Norad 0.18.4 FontInfo | SourceFormatData | Preserve the typed value unchanged; representative unowned name and PostScript fields are exercised by the allowlist regression. |
| features.fea | Canonical per-source metadata | Preserve exact text; Save As also relocates recursively resolved relative include files. |
| groups.plist and kerning.plist | Canonical per-source metadata | Preserve all valid groups, member order, typed pair spelling and exact finite f64 values. |
| lib.plist entries for public.skipExportGlyphs and public.openTypeCategories that name loaded glyphs | Canonical per-source glyph metadata for semantics; SourceFormatData for source ordering | Canonical values control edits; the glyph-free boundary record preserves list order, source spelling and unknown-name entries. |
| Entries in those two standard dictionaries that do not name a loaded glyph, plus every other font-lib key | SourceFormatData | Preserve exact plist values and merge canonical entries without overwriting residual entries. |
| Layer order, layer names, glyph-directory paths, layer color and layer lib | SourceFormatData, addressed by canonical LayerId | Preserve order and exact persistence paths while canonical source/layer structure owns editable association. |
| Glyph name and layer membership | Canonical Project glyph/source structure | Structural operations update stable identities and rebuild the corresponding GLIF set. |
| Contours, point coordinates/types/smooth state, components, anchors and their paint order | Canonical Babelfont geometry | Export from canonical geometry without a persistent UFO glyph owner. |
| Horizontal and vertical advances, Unicode order, note, guidelines, image placement and residual glyph lib | Layer preservation | Retain exact values beside the stable layer identity and merge known keys only at export. |
| Contour, point, component, anchor and guideline identifiers, names, colors, transforms and object libs | Layer preservation keyed by stable object identity | Reorder moves metadata with identity; replacement retains metadata only through an explicit mapping. |
| Mark color, metrics formulas, composition recipe, metaballs, smart-component values and poles, HOI intermediates, editable hyperbezier kind and mask encoding | Typed or validated layer preservation | Decode known keys once, retain their exact supported source representation and write each key once at export. |
| images/ and data/ resource names and bytes | SourceFormatData | Preserve exact relative names and bytes; image placement is a separate layer value. |
| Exact contents.plist GLIF filenames | Filesystem preservation | Restore validated relative paths after staging and verify the staged font reloads with them. |
| Regular files outside Norad-managed UFO files, images/ and data/ | Filesystem preservation | Copy bytes unchanged into the staged UFO. |

## Designspace allowlist

Every accepted Designspace field is canonical; there is no opaque XML fallback.
The checked XML reader rejects unknown structure before Norad can ignore it.

| Designspace field family | Canonical owner |
|---|---|
| Format version | CanonicalDesignspace |
| Continuous axes: name, tag, explicit or implicit minimum/maximum, default, hidden flag, ordered map and localized labels | CanonicalAxis |
| Full sources: order, family/style/name, filename and sparse user-or-design location | SourceDescriptor plus CanonicalLocation |
| Layer-only sparse sources: order, owning UFO/layer, family/style/name and location | SparseSourceDescriptor plus SourceOrderEntry |
| Instances: order, family/style/name, filename, PostScript name, style-map names, location and instance lib | CanonicalInstance |
| Rules: processing order, names, ordered condition sets, bounds and substitutions | CanonicalRule |
| Top-level lib | CanonicalDesignspace opaque plist dictionary |
| Presence of an empty axis-mappings container | CanonicalDesignspace preservation flag |

formats::designspace validates the XML element and attribute allowlist before typed decoding, and every persisted coordinate must round-trip through Norad's f32 representation.

## Intentional rejection boundary

The adapter intentionally returns an error for these inputs instead of attempting a lossy save:

- unknown Designspace elements or attributes outside plist lib contents;
- nonempty cross-axis mappings and discrete-axis values;
- anisotropic or ambiguous locations, unknown or duplicate dimensions, missing values and nonfinite coordinates;
- Designspace numeric spellings that cannot round-trip through the current Norad codec;
- duplicate axis names/tags, duplicate full-source files or locations, a missing mapped-default source, and layer sources without their owning UFO/layer;
- malformed canonical UFO metadata, including invalid group or kerning names, nonfinite kerning, invalid font metrics, duplicate/non-string skip-export values and non-string OpenType category values;
- UFO symbolic links, non-regular filesystem entries, unsafe preserved GLIF paths and overlapping or aliased export destinations;
- unsupported imported-format fields already documented by the Glyphs, compiled-font and Python Babelfont adapters.

Rust Babelfont JSON remains unsupported.
The Python Babelfont directory importer is a separate checked conversion contract and never rewrites its source package.


## Exporting
https://runebender.org/docs/exporting.html

Export compiles the font as it is on screen, with fontc built into the editor, and writes a TTF file.

### Export

Press Cmd+Alt+E, or use File → Export….

Runebender compiles the font as it is in the editor, unsaved edits
included. It does not save your sources first, and it does not change
them.

The output is exports/.ttf in the directory that holds your
source. For Font.designspace, that is exports/Font.ttf. The footer
says where the file went, or why the export failed.

In the browser, Export downloads the TTF file.

### How It Compiles

The compiler is [fontc](https://github.com/googlefonts/fontc), built
into Runebender as a library. You do not install anything. Export does
not run a build script, a separate fontc program, or Python.

The live preview uses the same compiler, so the exported font matches
what the preview shows.

Runebender does not apply production names from
public.postscriptNames. The glyph names in the exported
font are the names in your source.

If your project has its own build script, run it yourself to make
release builds.

### From the Command Line

runebender compile compiles a UFO or designspace with the same
pipeline. It reads the source and does not change it.

    runebender compile Font.designspace --out Font.ttf

### Single Glyphs

Glyph → Export Glyph as SVG writes the current glyph as an SVG file
beside the source. It is for a drawing you want outside the font, not
part of the font build.


## Themes
https://runebender.org/docs/themes.html

Make, install, and share Runebender themes with the Base UI and Rainbow palettes.

A Runebender theme is one portable .theme.toml file.
The bundled themes are in [assets/themes/default](https://github.com/fontgarden/runebender/tree/main/assets/themes/default).
The native editor reads installed files at startup; the browser bundles the seven built-in themes: Dark, Gray, Light, Dark Gray, Light Gray, Strawberry, and Campfire.
The format has formatVersion = 1 so future versions can change without guessing how to read an older file.
Existing .theme.json files still load.

## The two palettes

| Name | TOML section | What to say when requesting a change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Base UI** | baseUi | “Make Base UI 07 warmer.” Ten numbered stops, 00–09, progress from darkest to lightest in the built-in themes. A custom theme can tint or replace each stop. |
| **Rainbow** | rainbow | “Change Rainbow red.” Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, and pink are stable mark categories; teal is also available for editor roles. Each hue has dim, base, bright, and deep steps. |

surfaces, text, and roles say where those palette colors are used.
For example, gray.roles.pointSmooth is rainbow.blue.base, while gray.surfaces.panel is baseUi.07.
Each theme chooses its ten Base UI colors; Gray starts at dark gray rather than black.
Built-in surfaces and text reference this scale instead of adding separate neutral colors.
Existing custom themes with longer scales still load.
The earlier glyphGrid section name and color references remain supported for existing themes.
A role can also use an explicit color such as #AABBCC.
The theme's markStep chooses which Rainbow step appears on glyph cells.

Runebender writes simple canonical public.markColor values to UFO files (1,0,0,1 for red, for example).
These values are compatibility tags, not display colors; each theme controls the visible Rainbow palette.
The editor still recognizes older values already saved in UFOs.

## Make and use a theme

```sh
runebender theme init --from gray --id my-theme --name "My Theme" --out my-theme.theme.toml
runebender theme validate my-theme.theme.toml
RUNEBENDER_THEME_PATH="$PWD/my-theme.theme.toml" RUNEBENDER_THEME=my-theme runebender
```

The init command creates a new file and never overwrites an existing one.
Use --from light or --from dark to start from those built-in themes.
runebender theme list and runebender --json theme list show discovered themes.
The native View → Theme menu includes installed themes, and Cycle Theme visits them after the built-ins.
Restart the editor after editing a theme file.

The native editor searches $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/runebender/themes/, or ~/.config/runebender/themes/ when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is unset.
It reads files ending in .theme.toml or .theme.json directly in that directory.
RUNEBENDER_THEME_PATH adds one file or a platform-separated list of files and directories.
These paths can point into a Git checkout or a dotfiles repository; a symlink in the config directory works too.
RUNEBENDER_THEME selects an installed theme by its id.
An unknown ID uses Gray and prints a diagnostic.
Invalid files are skipped with a path and error message; they do not prevent the editor from opening.
Installed IDs must be unique, use only ASCII letters, digits, - or _, and contain at most 64 characters.
Display names must contain 1–80 visible characters.

## Edit the file

Each theme file owns its Base UI stops, Rainbow hues and steps, surface colors, text colors, semantic roles, point and mark styles, and geometry.
Base UI and Rainbow hues use oklch(lightness chroma hue) color strings.
Lightness runs from 0 to 1, chroma describes color intensity from 0 upward with no fixed maximum, and hue runs around the color wheel from 0 to 360 degrees.
Rainbow steps use the same notation for signed offsets rather than complete colors.
For example, bright = "oklch(0.13 -0.03 0)" adds 0.13 lightness, subtracts 0.03 chroma, and leaves the hue unchanged.
The original component-table form remains supported for existing themes.
It does not depend on another theme file, so one file is enough to share a theme.
Sections and keys work like Cargo.toml, and # starts a comment.

```toml
formatVersion = 1
id = "my-theme"
name = "My Theme"

[baseUi]
"07" = "#AABBCC"

[surfaces]
panel = "baseUi.07"
```

This excerpt shows the syntax; copy a bundled theme for all required values.
The built-ins use oklch(L C H) values, with lightness L from 0 to 1 and hue H in degrees.
You can also use #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA for a Base UI stop or a direct surface, text, or role value.
References use baseUi.00 or rainbow.red.base syntax.
The parser reports missing roles, bad references, unsupported format versions, and invalid colors by theme and key.
Unknown fields are rejected so misspelled settings do not silently disappear.

The shape fields in geometry are pixel measurements: radius, radiusControl, stroke, and strokeEmphasis.
radius rounds glyph tiles and popup surfaces; radiusControl rounds buttons and fields.
Set both to 0 for square geometry, or both to 4 for gently rounded geometry.
Circular mark swatches and icons retain their own shapes.
markStyle is fill or border; pointStyle is fill or ring.
markOutline, markInk, and pointOutline are optional colors; pointHalo is a boolean.
All seven named Rainbow marks must remain in rainbow.marks exactly once, because glyph mark names are saved font metadata.

Start a color change at the use site under src/application/view/, then follow its named color in src/application/design/theme.rs to the file's surfaces, text, or roles section.
src/ui/theme.rs is the toolkit-independent parser and resolver.
src/application/platform/themes.rs discovers native files.
Check Gray and Light captures at the same size after a built-in change.

## Sharing and external desktop themes

A theme repository can contain its .theme.toml file, a preview image, and a README; Runebender needs only the TOML file.
This is enough to share through GitHub or dotfiles and gives a future gallery a stable file to index.
Do not download and execute code to install a color theme.

An Omarchy theme repository can keep a Runebender .theme.toml beside its colors.toml, then expose that file through RUNEBENDER_THEME_PATH or a config-directory symlink.
The two formats are separate today; Runebender does not automatically read colors.toml or follow Omarchy theme switches.
A small generator or Omarchy template can translate its color values into Runebender's Base UI stops later, without changing Runebender's file format.


## Scripting
https://runebender.org/docs/scripting.html

Use Python recipes, live MCP tools, saved-source scripts, or the Rust font engine.

### Choose an Automation Surface

| Surface | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| Python recipes | Explicit single-source edits and proofs from the native Scripts workflow. |
| [Live MCP](/docs/mcp.html) | Inspecting unsaved editor state, proposals, receipt-backed edits, and proof jobs. |
| Saved-source scripts | Repeatable batch work on UFO and Designspace files. |
| Rust font engine | Purpose-built tools that use the editor's canonical operations without a window. |

The editor has an optional external Python interpreter for recipes.
The editor itself does not require Python, and the subprocess boundary is not an operating-system sandbox.
For a guarded live edit, use the receipt and revision rules in [MCP](/docs/mcp.html).

### Saved Sources

A script can write UFO files while the native editor is open.
The editor watches files and reloads changes when they do not conflict with unsaved work.
Coordinate writes and keep sources in version control.
A disk script cannot read an unsaved outline on the canvas; use the live connection for that state.

### Current Limits

Python recipes currently mutate one explicit source at a time with bounded guarded operations.
Cross-source and whole-font atomic recipes are not implemented.
Live MCP capabilities differ from saved-source commands, and exact tool availability comes from tools/list in the connected session.


## Known limitations
https://runebender.org/docs/known-limitations.html

What Runebender currently supports and what its checks do not prove.

Runebender is experimental.
Keep font sources in version control and work on copies when evaluating a new build.

## Platforms and input

Native Linux and macOS compile, lint, document, and test in CI.
Most hands-on interaction work has been on macOS; Linux pointer, IME, file-dialog, accessibility, and GPU combinations need more supervised checks.
The Windows build and headless commands have passed basic checks, but native startup has failed in the [Windows workflow](https://github.com/fontgarden/runebender/actions/workflows/windows.yml).
The live editor endpoint uses Unix sockets and is unavailable on Windows.
Headless file commands remain portable.

## Browser

The browser build reuses the Xilem/Masonry interface.
It opens and saves UFO and designspace folders only in browsers with the File System Access API, such as Chrome and Edge.
Other browsers edit the bundled font in memory.
It has no microphone access, so Talk is unavailable, and local AI servers do not run in the browser.
The browser workspace pins the same Xilem revision as the desktop build, and web/prepare.py moves that pin with it.
The published browser build can still lag the native editor until the site is rebuilt.
In other browsers, reloading discards edits.
Native accessibility forwarding, local subprocesses, and native live-agent access require the desktop application.
Chromium tests do not certify Safari, Firefox, platform IMEs, or native GPU behavior.

## Font formats

The canonical Project owns editable glyph and source data, with UFO-only values preserved at explicit adapter boundaries.
Unsupported Designspace extensions, discrete axes, cross-axis mappings, anisotropic locations, and layer-only UFOs without a full source fail explicitly.
Interpolation requires compatible contours, components, and anchors.
Auxiliary layers are editable but do not automatically become interpolation sources.
The compiler emits TrueType variations; VARC and exhaustive UFO/OpenType metadata parity are not claimed.
See [Source format preservation](/docs/source-format-allowlist.html) for the accepted field families.

## Agent and proof checks

The live endpoint reads the unsaved canonical document, but unfinished pointer gestures are private until committed.
Receipt-backed edits are bounded to one explicit source and their receipts last only for that document lifetime.
A successful proof transport does not establish that a particular model received or interpreted the image.
Use connected MCP tools/list for exact tool schemas and [MCP](/docs/mcp.html) for the workflow.


## Troubleshooting
https://runebender.org/docs/troubleshooting.html

What to check when the editor will not build, will not open a font, or does something unexpected.

### It Will Not Build

Build in a clone to use the pinned toolchain, or pass +stable when installing.
Runebender requires Rust 1.96 or newer. Check the repository README for your
platform's system libraries.

```sh
cargo install --git https://github.com/fontgarden/runebender
```

If it still fails, include the first compiler error, Rust version, operating
system, and application revision in your report.

### A Font Will Not Open

Runebender opens .designspace files, .ufo directories, and folders
that hold them. It does not open compiled .ttf or .otf files.

A designspace that names a master file which is not there will not
open. Check the filename of each source in the designspace.

### A Glyph Will Not Interpolate

Interpolation needs matching outlines across masters: the same number
of contours, the same number of points in each, in the same order,
starting at the same point.

1. Run Path → Correct Path Direction in each master.
2. Use Path → Set Start Point so each contour starts in the same place.
3. Run Path → Tidy Up Paths to remove zero-length segments, which
differ between masters without being visible.
4. Compare the point counts in the Masters section.

### A Word Does Not Join

Cursive scripts find their joining forms by glyph name. A misnamed
glyph looks to a shaping engine like a missing one.

Run Glyph → Check Joining. It reports which of the initial, medial,
final, and isolated forms are present and whether the names follow
the expected convention.

### The Browser Build

The [WASM editor](/wasm-editor/) opens the bundled font, and in Chrome and Edge it opens and saves your own UFO or designspace folders.
In other browsers, reloading resets the edits. Local AI needs the desktop application.
See [Development](/docs/development.html) for the current browser milestone.

### Reporting a Problem

Open an issue on
[the repository](https://github.com/fontgarden/runebender/issues).

A useful report says what you did, what happened, and what you
expected. Name the file you had open and whether you were in the
browser or the native application. If the editor wrote something
wrong into a source, the diff from version control is the best
evidence there is.


## Architecture
https://runebender.org/docs/architecture.html

One application package with a reusable font engine and a shared browser view tree.

Runebender's root runebender Cargo package builds the native editor, headless commands, and font-engine library.
The separate web/ Cargo workspace reuses the application view tree with an in-memory browser host.
Sibling repositories are independent projects.

## Source map

| Path | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| src/lib.rs | Font-engine module root. |
| src/main.rs | Executable composition root. |
| src/font/ | Canonical Project, source operations, history, persistence, interpolation, and compilation. |
| src/outline/, src/text/, src/analysis/ | Reusable geometry, shaping, and measurement. |
| src/formats/ | Source-format adapters and persistent metadata. |
| src/automation/ | Agent and live-editor operation contracts. |
| src/workflows/, src/ui/ | Saved workflows and toolkit-independent editor data. |
| src/application/editor/ | User intent, commands, sessions, and tools. |
| src/application/view/ | Xilem views, panels, and canvas. |
| src/application/design/ | Theme palette, design tokens, control states, and recipes. |
| src/application/platform/ | Files, dialogs, watching, live IPC, and screenshots. |
| web/ | Browser host for the shared widgets. |

Read the relevant module header before changing code.
The repository's AGENTS.md carries local working rules and validation constraints.

## Ownership

font::project::Project is the authoritative in-memory document.
Babelfont owns canonical glyph geometry.
Stable layer and object identities retain exact UFO-only values that Babelfont cannot express.
Norad values are constructed at explicit import, export, and serialization boundaries; they are not a second live font model.

Views read workspace state and dispatch commands.
Application editor code interprets gestures and user intent.
Reusable font behavior belongs in the engine, which has no Xilem, Masonry, dialog, or window dependency.
Native and browser editing use the same canonical operations.

## Change routing

| Change | Start with |
| --- | --- |
| Editor tool or shortcut | src/application/editor/tools/, src/application/actions.rs |
| Canvas or panel | src/application/view/canvas/, src/application/view/panels/ |
| Theme or reusable control | assets/themes/default/, src/application/design/theme.rs, design/tokens.rs, design/recipes/ |
| Glyph outline or interpolation | src/outline/, src/font/ |
| UFO or Designspace preservation | src/font/persistence/, src/formats/ |
| Live agent tool | src/automation/, src/application/platform/live*.rs |
| Browser behavior | web/, then the shared application source |

The full file tree is in the [source repository](https://github.com/fontgarden/runebender).
For build checks and interface work, see [Development](/docs/development.html) and [Design principles](/docs/design-principles.html).


## Development
https://runebender.org/docs/development.html

Build and contribute to Runebender.

### Source and Build

[runebender](https://github.com/fontgarden/runebender) contains the editor and its font engine in the root Cargo package.
The repository pins its Rust toolchain.
Start with its AGENTS.md, then use [Code Layout](/docs/code-layout.html) and the [architecture guide](/docs/architecture.html) to find the right module.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/fontgarden/runebender
cd runebender
cargo run --profile fast --locked -- path/to/Font.designspace
```

The fast profile is intended for local UI development.
Cargo builds when needed, then launches the editor; the executable is target/fast/runebender.
This profile keeps release's optimization level and disabled debug assertions, while disabling LTO and enabling incremental compilation with 16 code-generation units to favor shorter rebuilds.
The first build fills a separate cache.
Runtime performance may differ from release, so use cargo run --release --locked -- path/to/Font.designspace for release performance comparisons.
The --locked flag keeps dependency versions fixed to the committed Cargo.lock.

### Checks

Use focused checks while iterating and run broader checks relevant to the change before finishing.
The full native CI suite is:

```sh
cargo fmt --all --check
bash .github/scripts/copyright.sh
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --locked
cargo test --workspace --locked -- --test-threads=1
cargo build --workspace --release --locked
cargo deny --locked check advisories
```

The root toolchain is pinned in rust-toolchain.toml.
CI runs on Linux and macOS with warnings denied.
Windows has a diagnostic workflow; see [Known limitations](/docs/known-limitations.html).
Some tests need the adjacent Virtua Grotesk checkout or RUNEBENDER_TEST_FONTS pointing to a source directory.
Do not count ignored model tests as passing model coverage.

### Interface Work

Read the [design principles](/docs/design-principles.html) and [themes](/docs/themes.html) before changing a view.
Use headless captures in Gray and Light for visual checks, then perform native interaction checks when the change needs pointer, keyboard, IME, accessibility, or GPU evidence.
The browser reuses the desktop widget tree; changes that affect it need the checks in the repository's web/README.md.

### License

Apache-2.0 or MIT.


## Code Layout
https://runebender.org/docs/code-layout.html

Find the current implementation in the runebender repository.

### One Application Package

The root runebender Cargo package contains the native editor, headless commands, and reusable font engine.
The browser host is a separate Cargo workspace under web/ and reuses the editor sources.
The complete [architecture guide](/docs/architecture.html) is the source map and change-routing guide.

### Where to Start

| Area | Source |
| --- | --- |
| Executable and CLI | src/main.rs, src/application/cli.rs |
| Native application state and editing | src/application/workspace.rs, src/application/editor/ |
| Views, canvas, and controls | src/application/view/, src/application/widgets/ |
| Platform adapters | src/application/platform/ |
| Canonical document and persistence | src/font/ |
| Agent and live editing contracts | src/automation/ |
| Outline, text, formats, and analysis | src/outline/, src/text/, src/formats/, src/analysis/ |
| Toolkit-independent UI data and workflows | src/ui/, src/workflows/ |
| Browser host | web/ |

The in-memory document is font::project::Project.
Babelfont owns canonical glyph geometry; UFO and Designspace adapters preserve values that are not represented there.

### Before Editing

Read the repository's AGENTS.md for local working rules.
For interface changes, read [interface design principles](/docs/design-principles.html) and [themes](/docs/themes.html).
Use [Development](/docs/development.html) for build and validation commands.


## Configuration
https://runebender.org/docs/configuration.html

Choose a theme, local model directories, and helper programs with environment variables.

### Themes

RUNEBENDER_THEME selects a built-in or installed theme by ID.
RUNEBENDER_THEME_PATH adds one theme file or a platform-separated list of files and directories.
The native editor also discovers .theme.toml and existing .theme.json files in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/runebender/themes/, or ~/.config/runebender/themes/ when that variable is unset.
An unknown theme ID falls back to Gray with a diagnostic.
See [Themes](/docs/themes.html) for the format, installation, and sharing workflow.

```sh
RUNEBENDER_THEME_PATH="$PWD/my-theme.theme.toml" RUNEBENDER_THEME=my-theme runebender
```

### Local Models

The default model directory is ~/Runebender/models.
RUNEBENDER_MODELS overrides it.
Runebender still reads models from the older ~/.runebender/models, but never writes there.

To look for models in more directories, list them one per line in ~/.runebender/model_paths, or set RUNEBENDER_MODEL_PATHS to a platform-separated list.

Other variables:
- RUNEBENDER_LLAMA_SERVER: Path to a llama-server program, used when the application has no bundled copy.
- RUNEBENDER_WHISPER_SERVER: Path to a whisper-server program, used when the application has no bundled copy.
- RUNEBENDER_WHISPER_MODEL: Path to the Whisper model file for voice input.
- RUNEBENDER_CONTEXT_PATH: More directories of personal design context files, after ~/.config/runebender/context/.

See [Local Models](/docs/local-models.html) for setup and current capabilities.

### What Is Not a Config File

Runebender currently does not read the ~/.config/runebender/config.toml settings previously described here.
Use the documented environment variables and theme files.
For exact available options, inspect the current [application source](https://github.com/fontgarden/runebender/tree/main/src/application) or run the executable's help command.


## FAQ
https://runebender.org/docs/faq.html

Short answers, including the uncomfortable ones.

### The Project

What it is:
- Is it ready for production work?: No. It is alpha. It writes to your sources in place, so keep them in version control and work on copies.
- What does it cost?: Nothing. Apache-2.0 or MIT.
- Is this an official Linebender project?: No. It is built on Linebender crates and aims at the Linebender stack, but the site and the editor are maintained independently.
- Where is the source?: runebender contains the application.

### Files

Formats:
- What can it open?: UFO, designspace, .glyphs, .glyphspackage, and compiled .ttf or .otf. See Opening and Saving.
- Can it write .glyphs?: No. Glyphs files are converted to UFO on the way in, and you work on the converted files.
- Will it overwrite my .ttf?: No. A compiled font opens as a UFO in memory, and saving writes that UFO beside the binary.
- Does it read FontLab or FontForge sources?: No.
- Can another editor open what it saves?: Yes. It writes standard UFO, and uses the glyphsLib keys for Glyphs-compatible data rather than inventing its own. See File Format.

### Running It

Install and launch:
- Is there a download?: Not yet. Build runebender with cargo. See Install.
- Can I use it in a browser?: Yes. The WASM editor opens with a bundled font. In Chrome and Edge, File → Open picks a UFO or designspace folder on your computer, and Save writes it back. Other browsers keep the bundled font only.
- Windows and Linux?: The code is cross-platform and builds there, but macOS is where it is used daily and where problems get found first.

### Drawing

Common confusions:
- Why will my glyph not interpolate?: The masters disagree about contour count, point count, point order, or start point. See Concepts and Checking a Font.
- What is a hyperbezier?: A curve defined by the points you place, with the handles solved rather than positioned. Convert to cubics before handing the source to a tool that expects them.
- Why does my Arabic not join?: Usually glyph names. Shaping engines find joining forms by name. Run Glyph → Check Joining. See Text and Shaping.
- Can I script it?: Yes. The native Scripts workflow supports optional Python recipes, and saved-source scripts can work beside the editor. See Scripting.
- Does it use AI?: It can run a model on your machine, over your sources, with nothing sent anywhere. One job so far: proposing a heavier master from a lighter one. It is experimental and often wrong. See Local Models.

### Getting Help

Open an issue on
[the repository](https://github.com/fontgarden/runebender/issues).
A useful report says what you did, what happened, and what you
expected, and names the file and whether you were in the browser or
the native application. If the editor wrote something wrong into a
source, the diff from version control is the best evidence there is.


## Interface design principles
https://runebender.org/docs/design-principles.html

Keep the glyph primary and the application state legible.

Runebender is a dense working tool for type design.
Controls should remain stable while values change, and decoration should never obscure the active glyph.
Other editors are references to evaluate, not feature lists to copy.

## Use named roles

Colors come from installed .theme.toml files and are resolved through src/application/design/theme.rs.
The [theme guide](/docs/themes.html) names the Base UI and Rainbow palettes.
Spacing, sizes, radii, strokes, and type come from src/application/design/tokens.rs.
Repeated controls belong in src/application/design/recipes/.
A new color needs a named role in every built-in theme.

## Keep the interface steady

- Align controls to shared sizes and keep sibling spacing in one place.
- Do not make panels jump or reorder under the pointer as content changes.
- Keep canvas marks thin and relevant to the active edit.
- Let chrome describe application state without covering the drawing.
- Use title case for titles and captions, never all caps. Commands are verbs and labels are nouns.
- Error text says what failed and what the user can do next.

## Check the actual result

For ordinary interface changes, inspect only the default theme (currently Gray).
Check other themes at the same size when working on themes or when explicitly requested.
A headless capture shows the rendered widget tree but does not prove pointer, keyboard, IME, accessibility, or GPU behavior.
Run a native interaction check when the change affects those paths.
The repository's AGENTS.md and CI define the current code checks.


## Glossary
https://runebender.org/docs/glossary.html

Terms used across these pages, in the sense Runebender uses them.

### Sources

Files and formats:
- UFO: Unified Font Object. A font source made of directories and files, so it works with version control.
- GLIF: The XML file that holds one glyph inside a UFO.
- Designspace: A file that names several masters and the axes between them.
- Master: One drawn source at a fixed position in the designspace.
- Axis: A dimension of variation, such as weight or width.

### Drawing

Outlines:
- Contour: One closed or open path in a glyph.
- On-curve point: A point the outline passes through.
- Handle: An off-curve control point that shapes the segment beside it.
- Cubic: A curve with two handles per segment. What UFO and PostScript use.
- Quadratic: A curve with one handle per segment. What TrueType uses.
- Hyperbezier: A curve defined by its on-curve points, with the handles solved rather than placed.
- Extreme: The topmost, bottommost, leftmost, or rightmost point of a curve.
- Path direction: Which way a contour is drawn. Outer contours and holes must run opposite ways.
- Start point: The first point of a contour. Masters must agree on it to interpolate.

### Building Glyphs

Composites:
- Component: Another glyph placed inside this one.
- Composite: A glyph built from components rather than drawn.
- Decompose: Replace components with copies of their outlines.
- Anchor: A named point that says where a mark attaches.
- Smart component: A component that carries its own axes, so one component holds a range of shapes.

### Spacing and Text

Metrics and shaping:
- Advance width: How far the pen moves after drawing the glyph.
- Sidebearing: The space between the outline and the edge of the advance, left or right.
- Kerning: An adjustment applied to one pair of glyphs.
- Kerning group: A set of glyphs that kern alike, so one value covers many pairs.
- Shaping: Turning characters into positioned glyphs, applying the font's own rules.
- Bidirectional: Text that mixes directions, such as Arabic with Latin inside it.
- Joining form: The shape a cursive letter takes by position: initial, medial, final, or isolated.

### Output

Building a font:
- Compile: Turn sources into a font file a system can install.
- fontc: The Rust font compiler built into Runebender. Export and the live preview both use it.
- Production name: The glyph name that ships, which can differ from the working name.
- Variable font: One font file that holds a range along its axes rather than a single instance.
